title: Credential split by a literal LF or CRLF in plain text
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in plain text (a note, an email body, a log) is broken by a literal line feed or a carriage return plus line feed, with no construct that joins the lines.
rationale: Nothing rebuilds the value: the text holds two fragments and a separator, which is not the documented key grammar (fixed 69 characters, no separators). It is also a partial leak of a key-shaped value. The ambiguity: stripping whitespace to repair the key would be a global rewrite that turns arbitrary wrapped prose into a credential, and ignoring it may leave a half key in clear text.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 3 (#95)): expect it to be flagged. The provider documents the key as always 69 characters, which the separator-bearing text cannot satisfy, so the text is not a documented key. A key-shaped value split by a separator is a partial leak and is protected: the secret bytes are the fragments, the separator bytes are not secret. The engine scores the enclosing range, so separator bytes count as secret until it scores fragments. Synthetic, never issued: every value is built from the words SYNTHETIC and EXAMPLE. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: SendGrid API keys are always 69 characters long.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
